correctness.rationale: Choose the active coordinates uniformly, then sample independent signs and uniform simplex weights. A coordinate is active with probability s/d, and its conditional second moment is 2/[s(s+1)], so the affine kernel is 1+c x·y with c=d(s+1)/2. The row mass is convex on the entire polytope and equal at all vertices. Distinct vertex rows have opposite signs near the negative of one vertex on a set of positive skeletal measure, which makes every nontrivial combination strictly submaximal. The sign row attains the essential supremum by full support and continuity; L1 follows by symmetry. At a vertex the excess is (s/d) times the integral of (cU−1)_+ for U~Beta(1,s−1); integrating the tail (1−u)^(s−1) gives c/d times (1−1/c)^s, including s=1 by taking U=1. The logarithmic derivative in s+1 is strictly positive using log(1−u)>−u/(1−u) with u=2/[d(s+1)], and Taylor with bounded second derivative gives remainder at most s(s−1)/[d²(s+1)]≤1/d. Both limits and rational benchmarks follow. Replay: RESULT.md lines 32–93; verify.py and VERIFICATION.md describe 1,984 finite checks, inspected but not executed.
